findings.title: retryCount deletion branch not scoped to SMS method, risking deletion of unrelated WorkflowReminder rows
findings.body: The new `OR` clause in the `deleteMany` call adds `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method: SMS` constraint, while the original/sibling branch explicitly filters `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. Since `retryCount` is a column on the shared `WorkflowReminder` model used by EMAIL, SMS and WHATSAPP reminders alike, any reminder of any method that ends up with `retryCount > 1` (now or in a future change that reuses this column for other channels) will be silently deleted by this SMS-only cron endpoint. This conflates concerns and creates a latent data-integrity hazard: a future feature that increments `retryCount` for email/whatsapp reminders would have those reminders deleted by the SMS cron job. The condition should be `AND: [{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` to match the stated intent of only removing failed SMS reminders.

findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount increment can lose updates under concurrent/overlapping cron runs
findings.body: retryCount is incremented via `data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }`, using the value read earlier in the same request (from the initial `findMany`). If the cron job is triggered more than once concurrently (e.g., overlapping invocations due to a slow run or manual trigger plus scheduled trigger), two processes could read the same stale `retryCount` and both write the same incremented value, causing a lost update. This undermines the 'delete after two failures' guarantee the PR aims to provide. Using Prisma's atomic increment (`data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`) would avoid the race entirely and is low-cost to apply here and in the catch block below (line ~195).

findings.title: Overly broad catch block increments retryCount for unrelated failures, risking premature deletion of valid reminders
findings.body: The try block wraps not only the actual SMS-sending call (`twilio.scheduleSMS`) but also unrelated DB/network operations such as `prisma.profile.findFirst` and `getBookerBaseUrl`, and template rendering. Any transient failure in these unrelated steps (e.g., a brief DB hiccup or an external API blip while resolving the booker URL) increments `retryCount` exactly the same as a genuine SMS-provider failure such as an invalid phone number. Because the reminder is deleted once `retryCount > 1`, two unrelated/transient errors (not actual SMS failures) could cause a legitimate, sendable reminder to be permanently deleted before it ever had a real chance to be delivered. The retry/delete logic should be scoped specifically to the SMS send failure path rather than the entire per-reminder processing block.

findings.title: No automated tests added for new retry/deletion behavior
findings.body: This PR introduces non-trivial new behavior (incrementing retryCount on failure, and deleting reminders once retryCount exceeds the threshold) but no tests were added or updated to cover: (1) a failed `twilio.scheduleSMS` call incrementing retryCount, (2) an exception during processing incrementing retryCount, and (3) the deleteMany query correctly removing reminders once retryCount surpasses 1 while not catching reminders of other methods/states. Given this logic directly controls whether reminders are permanently deleted, lack of test coverage increases the risk of silent regressions.
